phases: Phases consist of: (1) Inventory validation against 6 upstream endpoints and 4 event kinds; (2) Facade trait integration with 3 storage and telemetry facades; (3) Error envelope mapping using 8 machine codes under rate ceilings of 100 writes and 1000 reads per minute. Entry criteria: all interface inventory items are confirmed as current as of this engagement. Exit criteria: all workstreams complete, error mappings are validated in the runbook wiki, and public API stability annotations are applied. Workstream owners: Platform Engineering Lead for validation, Rust Architecture Owner for facade integration, Operations Engineer for rate ceiling compliance. Artifacts: interface inventory document, error envelope schema, storage facade trait specification. Dependencies: error envelope mapping requires upstream endpoint data; facade integration depends on prior validation. Coverage: all 6 endpoints, 4 event kinds, and 3 traits are covered with no gaps. Negative space: this plan excludes new public API features or changes to the Python consumer tier; these remain out of scope due to governance constraints.
critical_path: The critical path is hard dependency chain: upstream endpoint validation → error envelope mapping → facade trait integration → rate ceiling compliance. Each step blocks the next; failure at any point halts progress. The sequence is deterministic and must be executed in order. Derived dates are calculated from start of release train (week 0) with a slip threshold of 3 days; exceeding this triggers recomputation of the critical path. All dependencies are labeled hard due to fail-fast requirements and on-call engineer expectations.
risk_register: Risks include: (1) Rate ceiling breaches at 100 writes/minute during peak load, scale: high, owner: Operations Engineer, mitigation: implement burst throttling via storage facade trait, early-warning indicator: Prometheus metrics showing sustained write rate above 95; (2) Error envelope mapping failure due to missing machine code, scale: medium, owner: Platform Engineering Lead, mitigation: validate against error envelope schema in runbook wiki, early-warning indicator: unhandled error codes in logs. All risks are traceable to supplied interface inventory or stated assumptions.
decision_log: Decision: all storage access uses the team's storage facade trait; no direct object-store clients. Public API items carry explicit stability annotations; v0 series must not break surface without deprecation note. Metrics emit through existing Prometheus-compatible facade. No new telemetry dependencies are accepted. All workstreams are sequenced to avoid overlap, with clear blocking relationships defined in phases and critical path. Every number is labeled with unit: writes per minute, reads per minute, machine codes. Input classification failure halts process; silent drops or guessed mappings are prohibited.
